task.instruction: Discover three new and popular open-source NLP models for language translation released in the past month on Huggingface.

final_answer:
Here are three open-source translation models released on Hugging Face within the past month (Oct 7 – Nov 7, 2026), all tagged `translation` and traced back to their original release repos rather than counting quantized re-uploads as separate models:

**1. tencent/Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B** — created 2026-10-22 · 899 downloads · 47 likes (its FP8 build has 1,264 downloads and **461 likes**, making it the most-liked translation model released this month)
Tencent Hunyuan's real-time **simultaneous** translation model, supporting bidirectional **speech-to-speech translation between Chinese and English**: it continuously receives incoming audio and translates as the speaker talks, emitting both translated text and speech, with **real-time voice cloning** that preserves the speaker's vocal characteristics. Built for meetings, speeches and interviews where waiting for a finished sentence would disrupt the conversation. Apache-2.0, with FP8 and "Interleave" variants.

**2. pfnet/plamo-3-translate-8b** — created 2026-10-27 · 452 downloads · 12 likes (the 0.8B GGUF build has 14,380 downloads and 26 likes)
Preferred Networks' (PFN) translation-specialized LLM, built on PLaMo 3 NICT — a pretrained model from joint PFN–NICT research — and further trained on tens of billions of tokens of translation-focused data. It supports translation among **53 languages**, can take surrounding context and a glossary into account, and lets you choose plain vs. polite style for Japanese output. The family spans 0.8B / 2B / 8B / 31B sizes with GGUF, FP8, NVFP4, W4A16 and MLX-4bit variants. License: PLaMo Community License.

**3. IndexTeam/Index-Translate-omni-9B** — created 2026-11-04 · 1 like
A multimodal member of the Index-Translate family covering multilingual text translation, terminology and formatting constraints, **image translation, speech recognition, and bidirectional Chinese–English speech translation**. Its card reports FLORES COMET22 0.8789, WMT24++ COMET22 0.8601 and WMT26 Judge 75.35 — matching the text-only Index-Translate 9B — with the larger Omni 35BA3B reaching 78.01 on WMT26 Judge. Siblings include 2B and 35B sizes plus FP8 and GGUF builds.

Honorable mention: **rikai-translate/rikai-jp-eng-Bench-265-1.4B** (2026-11-04, MIT) — a tiny on-device bidirectional Japanese↔English model fine-tuned from CAT-Translate-1.4b that matches or beats CAT-Translate-3.3B on most automatic metrics at 2.4× its decode speed (0.8425 on the 26-domain CometKiwi gate), shipped as fp16 safetensors plus an MLX 8-bit build.

judge.rationale: The third selected model has only 1 like and lacks shown open-source/license evidence, so the answer doesn’t satisfy “popular open-source” for three models.
